title: Ferlab-Ste-Justine/snv-post-processing pipeline parameters
description: Variant analysis for genome and exome GVCFs

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to the .csv sample file containing the Family ID, sample ID, sequencing Type and path to GVCF files
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns, and a header row.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

allow_intermediate_input.description: When re-starting from a subsequent step, allow the pipeline to use intermediate CSV files as input samplesheet when available.

reference_genome_options.title: Reference genome options
reference_genome_options.description: Reference genome related files and options required for the workflow.

genome.help_text:
If using a reference genome configured in the pipeline using iGenomes, use this parameter to give the ID for the reference. This is then used to build the full paths for all required reference genome files e.g. `--genome GRCh38`. 

See the [nf-core website docs](https://nf-co.re/usage/reference_genomes) for more details.

igenomes_ignore.description: Do not load the iGenomes reference config.
igenomes_ignore.help_text: Do not load `igenomes.config` when running the pipeline. You may choose this option if you observe clashes between custom parameters and those supplied in `igenomes.config`.

intervalsFile.help_text: Path to an interval file. If specified, will be used during the CombineGVCFs step to indicate the regions of interest.

referenceGenome.help_text: Contains the path to the directory that contains the reference fasta genome.

referenceGenomeFasta.description: Name of the fasta file for the genome
referenceGenomeFasta.help_text: Name of the fasta file for the genome we usually apply "Homo_sapiens_assembly38.fasta"

dbsnpFile.help_text: Path to dbsnp file. Will be used to add dbsnp ids in the output vcf ID column if provided.

dbsnpFileIndex.help_text: Path to dbsnp file index. Required if specifying the dbsnpFile parameter.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

max_job_request_options.title: Max job request options
max_job_request_options.description: Set the top limit for requested resources for any single job.
max_job_request_options.help_text:
If you are running on a smaller system, a pipeline step requesting more resources than are available may cause the Nextflow to stop the run with an error. These options allow you to cap the maximum resources requested by any single job so that the pipeline will run on your system.

Note that you can not _increase_ the resources requested by any job using these options. For that you will need your own configuration file. See [the nf-core website](https://nf-co.re/usage/configuration) for details.

max_cpus.description: Maximum number of CPUs that can be requested for any single job.
max_cpus.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the CPU requirement for each process. Should be an integer e.g. `--max_cpus 1`

max_memory.description: Maximum amount of memory that can be requested for any single job.
max_memory.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the memory requirement for each process. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--max_memory '8.GB'`

max_time.description: Maximum amount of time that can be requested for any single job.
max_time.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the time requirement for each process. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--max_time '2.h'`

max_disk.description: Maximum amount of disk space that can be requested for any single job.
max_disk.help_text: Use to set an upper-limit for the disk space requirement for each process. Should be a string in the format integer-unit e.g. `--max_disk '8.GB'`

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_all.description: Publish results from all processes to the output directory.
publish_all.help_text: If true (default false), publish results from all processes to the output directory. This is useful for debugging and testing, but can create a lot of output files.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

TSfilterSNP.help_text: Truth-sensitivity filter level for SNPs. This value is required by the VQSR step

TSfilterINDEL.help_text: This value is required by the VQSR step

hardFilters.help_text: Parameters for Hard-Filtering. Must be an array containing each desired filter. Each filter must be formatted with the desired name and expression, for example\n[[name: 'QD1', expression: 'QD < 1.0'],[name: 'QD2', expression: 'QD < 2.0]]

allow_old_gatk_data.description: Allow the use of old GATK data in GATK_GENOTYPEGVCFS process by adding --allow-old-rms-mapping-quality-annotation-data to ext.args. Note: this won't work if ext.args is overridden.
allow_old_gatk_data.help_text: Allow the use of old GATK data in GATK_GENOTYPEGVCFS process by adding --allow-old-rms-mapping-quality-annotation-data to ext.args. Note that this won't work if ext.args is overridden. This parameter is not recommended for production use.

tools.description: List of tools to use separate with comma.  Available tools: [vep, exomiser, slivar]

gvcf_filtering.description: If true (default), sanitize input gvcf files by removing malformed records (e.g. missing the required <NON_REF> allele) and duplicate-position records that cause compatibility issues with joint genotyping.
gvcf_filtering.help_text: If true (default), removes gVCF records missing the required <NON_REF> allele (a known defect in some DRAGEN gVCF outputs that otherwise makes GATK4_GENOTYPEGVCFS fail) and duplicate-position records. See usage documentation for more details.

step.description: Step from which to start the pipeline
step.help_text: Step to run. If not specified, pipeline will start from first step: genotype. If specified, pipeline will start from that step. When `inheritance` is selected, the input VCF is assumed to be already VEP-annotated.

save_genotyped.description: If true, publish the genotyped and normalized vcf files to the output directory.
save_genotyped.help_text: If true, save the normalized genotyped vcf files to the output directory. If false, only the final vcf files will be saved. Default when no tools are specified

broad.description: Directory containing the references for vqsr
broad.help_text:
Path to the directory containing 4 important files: 
1. The Hapmap file for vqsr training
2. The omni2.5 file for vqsr training
3. The 1000G SNP reference file for vqsr training
4. The dbsnp database for vqsr training

vqsr_snp_resources.description: Reference datasets for VQSR to build a model for filtering SNPs.
vqsr_snp_resources.help_text: List of `{labels, vcf, index}` maps. `labels` is the GATK `--resource:` label string (e.g. `hapmap,known=false,training=true,truth=true,prior=15`); `vcf` and `index` are paths to the training VCF and its index. Relative paths are resolved against `params.broad`; absolute paths are used as-is. Required when running VQSR on WGS data.

vqsr_snp_tranches.description: Truth-sensitivity tranches passed to VariantRecalibrator for SNPs.

vqsr_snp_annotations.description: Annotations (`-an`) used by VariantRecalibrator to build the SNP model.

vqsr_indel_resources.description: Reference datasets for VQSR to build a model for filtering INDELs.
vqsr_indel_resources.help_text: List of `{labels, vcf, index}` maps. Same shape as vqsr_snp_resources; see that param for details.

vqsr_indel_tranches.description: Truth-sensitivity tranches passed to VariantRecalibrator for INDELs.

vqsr_indel_annotations.description: Annotations (`-an`) used by VariantRecalibrator to build the INDEL model.

vep_cache.help_text: Path to the vepCache directory, which is usually installed by vep by default. It should contain at least the <cache_dir>/114_GRCh38/ directory, where <cache_dir> is `vep_species`, optionally suffixed with `_merged`/`_refseq` when `vep_annotation` is set (e.g. homo_sapiens, homo_sapiens_merged, homo_sapiens_refseq).

vep_cache_version.description: Which version of the vep cache to annotate with
vep_cache_version.help text: We recommend using the same version as vep, i.e. the vep version that matches the container.

vep_genome.description: Will be used by vep to find the assembly version in the cache

vep_species.description: Species VEP annotates against. Used as VEP's --species at the annotation step (always the plain species name — VEP rejects a _merged/_refseq suffix here) and, when `download_cache` is set, combined with `vep_annotation` as the species to download.

vep_annotation.description: Optional VEP cache flavor: 'merged' for the combined Ensembl/RefSeq cache, 'refseq' for the RefSeq-only cache. Leave unset for the default Ensembl-only cache.
vep_annotation.help_text: Sets VEP's --merged or --refseq flag at annotation time, and (when `download_cache` is set) selects the matching `<vep_species>_merged`/`<vep_species>_refseq` cache to download. When set to 'merged', the pipeline also adds VEP's --mane flag and the MANE/RefSeq-specific output fields automatically.

download_cache.description: Whether to download the vep cache (species/flavor/version/genome set via vep_species/vep_annotation/vep_cache_version/vep_genome) or use the one at vep_cache

outdir_cache.description: Path where vep cache will be downloaded. If not provided, will default to ${outdir}/cache.

vep_outdir.description: When specified, publishes the VEP output to this folder

exomiser_analysis_wes.description: Path to the exomiser analysis file (.yml) to use for whole exome sequencing input

exomiser_analysis_wgs.description: Path to the exomiser analysis file (.yml) to use for whole genome sequencing input

exomiser_data_dir.description: Path to the  exomiser data directory

exomiser_genome.description: Genome assembly version to be used by exomiser (e.g., hg38 or hg19)

exomiser_cadd_indel_filename.description: The filename of the exomiser CADD indel data file (e.g., gnomad.genomes.r4.0.indel.tsv.gz)

exomiser_cadd_snv_filename.description: The filename of the exomiser CADD snv data file (e.g., whole_genome_SNVs.tsv.gz)

exomiser_remm_filename.description: The filename of the exomiser REMM data file (e.g., ReMM.v0.3.1.post1.hg38.tsv.gz)

exomiser_local_frequency_path.description: Path to the local frequency data file. The `.tbi` index is assumed to live alongside (`<path>.tbi`) unless `exomiser_local_frequency_index_path` is set explicitly.

exomiser_local_frequency_index_path.description: Optional override for the tabix index of the local frequency data file. Defaults to `<exomiser_local_frequency_path>.tbi`.

exomiser_start_from_vep.description: If true, run the exomiser analysis on the VEP annotated VCF file

exomiser_outdir.description: When specified, publishes the exomiser output to this folder

slivar_options.title: Slivar options
slivar_options.description: Options for the slivar inheritance subworkflow, which tags variants by mode of inheritance and identifies compound heterozygotes from a VEP-annotated VCF and a PED file.

slivar_regions_bed.description: Optional BED file restricting slivar analysis to the specified regions.
slivar_regions_bed.help_text: When provided, passed to `slivar expr --regions`. Only variants overlapping these regions will be evaluated.

slivar_exclude_bed.description: Optional BED file of regions to exclude from slivar analysis.
slivar_exclude_bed.help_text: When provided, passed to `slivar expr --exclude`. Variants overlapping these regions are skipped (e.g., low-complexity or blacklist regions).

slivar_gnomad_gnotate.description: Path to the gnomAD slivar gnotate (.zip) file used to annotate gnomad_popmax_af and gnomad_nhomalt.
slivar_gnomad_gnotate.help_text: When provided, enables the gnomAD-based population-frequency guards in the slivar `--info` and `--family-expr` expressions. See https://github.com/brentp/slivar/wiki/gnotate for how to build this file.

slivar_topmed_gnotate.description: Path to the TOPMed slivar gnotate (.zip) file used to annotate topmed_af.
slivar_topmed_gnotate.help_text: When provided, enables the TOPMed-based population-frequency guard in the slivar `--info` expression.

slivar_js.description: JavaScript file defining helper functions used in the slivar expressions.
slivar_js.help_text: Defaults to the bundled `assets/slivar-functions.js`. Override only if you need custom segregation/quality functions.

skip_ped_validation.description: Run slivar even when a family's PED doesn't match its VCF, with warnings instead of stopping the run.
skip_ped_validation.help_text: By default the pipeline stops before slivar if a VCF sample has no row in the family's PED, or if a sequenced sample's father or mother is named in the PED but isn't in the VCF (write an unsequenced parent as `0`). Set this, e.g. for tests or exploratory runs, to report those problems as warnings and continue. slivar's inheritance and parental-origin tags may then be missing or wrong for the affected families.

gnomad_popmax_af_rare.description: Max gnomAD popmax allele frequency used in the general `--info` rare-variant filter.

topmed_af_rare.description: Max TOPMed allele frequency used in the general `--info` rare-variant filter.

gnomad_popmax_af_dominant.description: Max gnomAD popmax allele frequency for dominant and de novo inheritance calls.

gnomad_popmax_af_recessive.description: Max gnomAD popmax allele frequency for recessive inheritance calls.

gnomad_nhomalt.description: Max gnomAD homozygous-alt count allowed when tagging compound-het candidate sides.
